title: Amazon EventBridge: Event Buses, Pipes & Scheduler
summary: Route events between services and SaaS apps, connect sources to targets, and run schedules.
tldr: **Event bus + rules**: many producers, many consumers. Rules match on event content (including numeric ranges and prefixes) and route to targets. SaaS partners deliver straight to a **partner event bus**.
**Pipes**: one source to one target, with optional **filter**, **enrichment** and transformation in between. It replaces glue Lambda functions that poll SQS, Kinesis or DynamoDB Streams.
**Scheduler**: cron, rate and **one-time** schedules at massive scale, with time zones, retries and a DLQ. It's the answer for "run X at time T" without polling a database.

keyFacts.text: An **archive** on an event bus keeps events for a retention period you choose. A **replay** re-sends a time window of them, ideal after a consumer bug.
Turn on EventBridge notifications for a bucket to send every S3 event to the default bus. Then add rules per consumer instead of overlapping S3 notifications.
Scheduler and rule targets support a **retry policy** (maximum event age and retry attempts) and an **SQS dead-letter queue** for events that still fail.
Pipes read from polling sources such as **SQS, Kinesis, DynamoDB Streams, Amazon MQ and Kafka (MSK)**, then send to targets like Step Functions, SQS or an event bus.
An SQS delay queue or message timer can postpone delivery by at most 15 minutes. Longer delays (hours, days) call for **Scheduler one-time schedules**.

traps: Two S3 event notification configurations can't overlap on the same event type and prefix. Use EventBridge to fan out.
An EventBridge rule can't match "a message arriving in an SQS queue". Reading from a queue is a job for Pipes or a Lambda event source mapping.
DynamoDB TTL deletes items on a best-effort schedule, not at an exact time, so it is a poor timer.
A rule that runs every minute and scans a database is the polling design the question wants you to avoid.
SNS subscription filter policies filter messages, but SNS can't poll an SQS queue or enrich a message.
